R10-001-core-word.rationale: "assimilated" was replaced with "absorbed", producing the redundant "absorbed and absorbed" instead of two distinct processes (absorption then assimilation); overall meaning is still roughly conveyed but the duplication is confusing.

R10-001-core-sparse_common_sound.rationale: "smaller and smaller" became "least and finer" — "least" does not mean progressively smaller and does not parallel "finer", producing a semantically confusing phrase.

R10-001-calib-single_word.rationale: Same as the core-word variant: "assimilated" -> "absorbed" creates the redundant "absorbed and absorbed", losing the distinction between the two named processes.

R10-001-calib-word_plus_sound.rationale: Identical defect to the other single-word-change variants: "assimilated" replaced by "absorbed", yielding the redundant "absorbed and absorbed".

R10-001-calib-multi_sound.rationale: Same "least and finer" substitution for "smaller and smaller" seen in the sparse_common_sound variant — semantically wrong and confusing.

R10-001-calib-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: Same "least and finer" substitution for "smaller and smaller" — "least" does not function as a valid parallel comparative here.

R10-002-core-word.rationale: "esophagus" (noun) was replaced with "esophageal" (adjective only), leaving "swallow down the esophageal to enter the stomach" without a noun — ungrammatical and confusing to parse.

R10-003-core-word.rationale: "Peristalsis" and "esophagus" were turned into non-existent words ("Peristalaxis", "esophagum"), and "gastrointestinal tract" was narrowed to "intestines", excluding the esophagus/stomach the original term covered.

R10-004-core-word.rationale: "small bowel" is an accepted clinical synonym for "small intestine"; meaning is fully preserved.

R10-004-core-sparse_common_sound.rationale: "small intestine" is a fixed anatomical term; "little intestine" is not standard terminology, though the organ referred to remains clear.

R10-005-core-word.rationale: "reabsorbed" was replaced with "assumed", an unrelated word (meaning presumed) — "assumed back into the blood" is nonsensical.

R10-006-core-word.rationale: "two liquids" was changed to "two solids", reversing the physical claim (surfactants act between liquid interfaces, not solid-solid ones); additionally "surfactant"->"lubricant" and "surface tension"->"surface pressure" are wrong technical substitutions, and "emulsify"->"emollidate" is an invented word.

R10-007-core-word.rationale: "physiological" (organism-function specific) was flattened to "physical" (generic), losing precision, though the overall definition of nutrition still basically holds.

R10-007-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "support its life" became "give its life", which idiomatically means to sacrifice/lose one's life — nearly the opposite of sustaining life.

R10-007-calib-single_word.rationale: Same "physiological"->"physical" precision loss as the core-word variant.

R10-007-calib-multi_word.rationale: Restructured to "The nutritional process is the ... process by which...", a circular/redundant construction ("process is...process"), and "biochemical and physiological" was reordered to "biological and physiochemical" — awkward but meaning is still roughly recoverable.

R10-007-calib-word_plus_sound.rationale: "physiological process" became "physical act" — "act" implies a single action rather than an ongoing biological process, and "physical" again loses the biology-specific sense of "physiological".

R10-007-calib-multi_sound.rationale: Same as the dense_mixed_generic variant: "support its life" -> "give its life", idiomatically inverting the intended meaning of sustaining life.

R10-007-calib-sparse_common_sound.rationale: Same "support its life" -> "give its life" substitution, which idiomatically suggests sacrificing life rather than sustaining it.

R10-008-core-word.rationale: "hypertension"->"high blood pressure" is an accurate synonym and the remaining changes are cosmetic (hyphenation, pluralization); meaning fully preserved.

R10-008-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "stroke" was replaced with "shot", an unrelated word that does not belong in a list of diseases, producing a nonsensical item in the disease list.

R10-009-core-word.rationale: "molecules" was narrowed to "compounds" (compounds are a subset of molecules requiring two or more distinct elements), a minor taxonomic narrowing of the claim.

R10-010-core-word.rationale: "carbohydrates" was narrowed to "sugars" (sugars are only one subtype of carbohydrate, alongside starches and fiber), narrowing the scientific claim; "organisms"->"beings" is an acceptable synonym.

R10-011-core-word.rationale: "Nutrients" was changed to "Nutritions" — "nutrition" is an uncountable/abstract noun and pluralizing it this way is ungrammatical; "biochemical"->"biological" also loses precision.

R10-011-core-sparse_common_sound.rationale: "cells" was replaced with "cases", an unrelated word that makes "absorbed by the cases" nonsensical in this biological context.

R10-012-core-word.rationale: All substitutions ("deficiencies"/"can"/"incapacity"/"vital") are accurate synonyms; meaning fully preserved.

R10-012-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "sudden"->"quick" is a close enough synonym in this context; meaning is preserved.

R10-013-core-word.rationale: "rearranged" was shortened to "arranged", dropping the "re-" that conveys atoms being reconfigured from an existing state, a subtle but real meaning shift; "accompanied by"->"followed by" also shifts simultaneity to sequence.

R10-013-calib-single_word.rationale: "accompanied by" (simultaneous) became "followed by" (sequential/after), a subtle shift in the temporal relationship between the reaction and the energy change.

R10-013-calib-multi_word.rationale: "chemical reactions occur" became "chemical reaction occur" — singular subject with plural verb, a clear subject-verb agreement error; it also carries the "arranged"/"followed by" precision losses seen in other variants.

R10-013-calib-word_plus_sound.rationale: Same "accompanied by"->"followed by" temporal-nuance shift; "products"->"chemicals" is an acceptable loose synonym.

R10-014-core-word.rationale: "reactants" was corrupted into "reactionants", a non-existent word; the intended term is still inferable from context but is not valid English.

R10-014-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "Chemical reactions" became "Chemical answers" — "answers" is an unrelated word, making the sentence's subject nonsensical.

R10-015-core-word.rationale: The fixed term "activation energy" was changed to "activated energy", a non-standard variant of the technical term, though the overall meaning is still recoverable.

R10-016-core-word.rationale: "bimolecular" was rendered with an accent as "bimolécular", an incorrect spelling of the technical term; the restructuring of the sentence itself is fine and meaning-preserving.

R10-017-core-word.rationale: "reactions" was replaced with "results", removing the core chemistry concept (forward/reverse reactions) and leaving an incoherent claim that "results...differ in reaction rates".

R10-019-core-word.rationale: "straight line" was shortened to just "line", dropping a qualifier essential to Newton's first law (constant-speed motion along a curved line still involves acceleration), weakening the physical accuracy of the stated law.

R10-019-core-sparse_common_sound.rationale: "straight line" became "right line", an archaic term for straight line that a modern listener is likely to misread as "correct line" or a directional "right" line, creating ambiguity despite technically being an old synonym.

R10-020-core-word.rationale: "acceleration multiplied by its mass" became "accelerated mass", turning the product of two distinct quantities (F=ma) into a garbled single compound; separately, "momentum" was replaced by the vague "movement", dropping the specific physical quantity the rate-of-change definition depends on.

R10-020-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "the rate at which...is changing" became "the value at which...is changing" — "rate" (a change-per-time concept) is not equivalent to "value", making the statement imprecise though still roughly interpretable.

R10-021-core-word.rationale: "magnitude"->"size" and "opposite directions"->"opposing direction" are acceptable lay paraphrases; the core physical claim (equal size, opposite direction) is preserved.

R10-021-core-sparse_common_sound.rationale: "same magnitude" became "one magnitude", an unusual dialectal phrasing ("the one X" = "the same X") likely to read as confusing or ungrammatical to a general audience, even though the intended meaning is recoverable.

R10-022-core-word.rationale: "expresses the principle"->"states the rule" is an acceptable paraphrase; meaning fully preserved.

R10-022-core-multi_sound.rationale: "straight line" became "true line", a non-standard substitution that risks being read as "accurate/real line" rather than "straight"; "speed"->"velocity" is redundant with the line description but not itself a factual error.

R10-023-core-word.rationale: "does not accelerated" is an ungrammatical verb form (should be "accelerate"); additionally the fixed term "mechanical equilibrium" was replaced with the vaguer "physical balance".

R10-024-core-word.rationale: "of equal magnitude" became "of equal force", creating a circular/redundant phrase ("exerts force...of equal force") that is awkward though the intended meaning (equal-sized opposing forces) still comes through.

R10-024-core-dense_mixed_generic.rationale: "second"->"2nd" is purely a numeral-formatting change with no effect on meaning or spoken form.

R10-025-core-word.rationale: "held together by self-gravity" (gravity as an internal cohesive force) became "surrounded by self gravity" (gravity as an external envelope), reversing the physical relationship between the star's matter and its own gravity.
